decisions.decision: The six PRs were consolidated by merging origin/chore/apply-feedback, not by choosing between lineages
decisions.rationale: They were never divergent implementations. merge-base(HEAD, phase-09 lineage) is this branch's own 08-05 commit, and shared modules were byte-identical. chore/apply-feedback transitively contained main, #32, #38, #39 and #40, so a single merge collapsed the stack.

decisions.decision: A refusal proof asserts WHAT was thrown, never merely THAT something was
decisions.rationale: A feedback pass rewrote two refusal proofs as bare `throw: {}` leaves on the false premise that a .f.js module cannot catch — fjs/exec/module.f.js catches in shipped production code. The `throw:` form passes for any throw: mutating the tax-table refusal's `<` to `<=` still throws, via an unrelated path. Both content assertions are restored and carry MERGE NOTEs.

decisions.decision: A clean merge is verified by diffing proof-leaf sets of both parents against the result
decisions.rationale: The snapshot regression carried NO textual conflict and merged silently. A name-set diff is necessary but not sufficient — a leaf can keep its name and lose its assertions — so an assertion-count delta per changed file is checked too.

next_action: Phase 10 — Form 1040 Core, Line-16 Dispatch, and the Scope Guard (TAX-03/05/06/16). ROADMAP marks Research: YES (QDCGT and Schedule D Tax Worksheets). Alternatively clear backlog Phases 16-18.
context_notes: The consolidation blocker dissolved under measurement rather than needing a decision — the same way the earlier phase-7 merge question did. The lesson worth carrying: when branches look divergent, compute the merge-base and hash the shared files before treating it as a judgment call. The session's other finding is a refinement of the project's central rule: a green suite after a clean merge proves nothing either. Coverage can be lost with zero conflicts, so both parents' proof sets and per-file assertion counts are compared against the result. Still true and still the most valuable thing here: a red mutation means the tests and the code AGREE, not that the code is right.
